title: Reduce major cardiovascular events through approved obesity pharmacotherapy

concept.text: Demonstrate that an obesity medicine reduces cardiovascular death, myocardial infarction or stroke, beyond showing weight reduction. SELECT established this benefit for semaglutide in people with established cardiovascular disease and overweight or obesity, without diabetes. Proposed completion test: FDA cardiovascular-risk-reduction indication based on an event-driven randomized outcomes trial with the upper 95% confidence bound for the three-point MACE hazard ratio below 1. Test set by: FDA; SELECT prespecified the MACE composite. Its 17,604 participants supplied the decisive clinical-outcomes evidence. Reported achieved: FDA approved Wegovy's cardiovascular-risk-reduction indication on 8 March 2024; SELECT reported MACE in 6.5% versus 8.0%, hazard ratio 0.80. Overlaps: END-05, CAR-02. Sources given: [FDA cardiovascular indication announcement](https://www.fda.gov/news-events/press-announcements/fda-approves-first-treatment-reduce-risk-serious-heart-problems-specifically-adults-obesity-or) ; [FDA Wegovy label with SELECT results](https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/label/2024/215256s015lbl.pdf).

page.title: First obesity medicine approved to reduce major cardiovascular events
page.definition: An obesity medicine reduces the risk of cardiovascular death, nonfatal myocardial infarction (heart attack) or nonfatal stroke, evaluated as a composite, and a regulator approves it for that use in adults with established cardiovascular disease and overweight or obesity. This is secondary prevention; adults without cardiovascular disease are outside it.

goal.need: Weight reduction can accompany cardiovascular harm. SCOUT randomized 9,804 adults aged at least 55 years with overweight or obesity and cardiovascular disease, type 2 diabetes or both after a sibutramine run-in. Sibutramine produced further mean weight loss of 1.7 kg but increased cardiovascular events versus placebo: hazard ratio 1.16 (95% confidence interval 1.03–1.31). Cardiovascular event reduction therefore requires its own clinical test.

figures.caption: Cardiovascular outcomes in SCOUT, published on 2 September 2010.
figures.note: Mean treatment duration was 3.4 years. The composite included cardiovascular death, nonfatal myocardial infarction, nonfatal stroke and resuscitation after cardiac arrest.

statements.quote: Novo Nordisk also plans to initiate a cardiovascular outcomes study SELECT in approximately 17,500 people who are overweight or have obesity.
statements.context: The company's semaglutide obesity development programme.

statements.quote: Providing a treatment option that is proven to lower this cardiovascular risk is a major advance for public health.
statements.context: John Sharretts, director of FDA's Division of Diabetes, Lipid Disorders, and Obesity, discussing cardiovascular risk in adults with cardiovascular disease and overweight or obesity.

completion.title: FDA approves an obesity medicine to reduce major cardiovascular events in adults with cardiovascular disease.
completion.criterion: The US Food and Drug Administration approves, for a medicine it has approved for chronic weight management, an indication to reduce the risk of major adverse cardiovascular events (cardiovascular death, non-fatal myocardial infarction or non-fatal stroke) in adults with established cardiovascular disease and either obesity or overweight. The indication is based on a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled cardiovascular outcomes trial in that population. The first such approval was Wegovy (semaglutide 2.4 mg weekly) on 8 March 2024, based on SELECT: 17,604 adults without diabetes, events in 6.5% versus 8.0%, hazard ratio 0.80 (95% CI 0.72–0.90).
completion.set_by: US Food and Drug Administration, supplemental approval NDA 215256/S-011 and Wegovy prescribing information, section 1.
completion.threshold_quote: Wegovy is indicated in combination with a reduced calorie diet and increased physical activity to reduce the risk of major adverse cardiovascular events (cardiovascular death, non-fatal myocardial infarction, or non-fatal stroke) in adults with established cardiovascular disease and either obesity or overweight.
completion.basis: The breakthrough is a first: the FDA called Wegovy the first weight loss medication also approved to help prevent life-threatening cardiovascular events. The test names that event, its population and its pivotal trial; it is not a threshold fitted to a result. It covers secondary prevention only. A reduction of cardiovascular events in adults with obesity and no established cardiovascular disease is not part of this test.

milestones.title: An obesity medicine's laboratory and animal data support reasonably safe human testing.
milestones.criterion: Pharmacological and toxicological studies in laboratory animals or in vitro support the sponsor's conclusion that the proposed clinical investigations are reasonably safe, under 21 CFR 312.23(a)(8). FDA's semaglutide review, signed on 13 May 2021, records an existing standard nonclinical programme conducted and reviewed under IND 79754 and NDA 209637, subsequently reused for the obesity indication.
milestones.set_by: U.S. Food and Drug Administration, 21 CFR 312.23(a)(8), the general preclinical requirement for an investigational new drug application.
milestones.threshold_quote: reasonably safe to conduct the proposed clinical investigations.

milestones.title: An obesity medicine enters phase 1 testing in people.
milestones.criterion: The investigational medicine is administered to people in phase 1, FDA's initial introduction into humans. EMA's assessment dated 14 December 2017 lists semaglutide study 1820 as first-in-human testing: 56 healthy men, with single subcutaneous doses ranging from 0.625 to 80 µg/kg, assessing dose-escalation safety, pharmacokinetics and pharmacodynamics. This study belonged to semaglutide's diabetes development programme.
milestones.set_by: U.S. Food and Drug Administration, 21 CFR 312.21(a)(1), the general definition of phase 1; the cited semaglutide study preceded its obesity programme.
milestones.threshold_quote: Phase 1 includes the initial introduction of an investigational new drug into humans.

milestones.title: Semaglutide is superior to placebo on both STEP 1 weight endpoints at 68 weeks, with two-sided P<0.05.
milestones.criterion: Both prespecified coprimary endpoints favor semaglutide at two-sided P<0.05: percentage weight change and the proportion losing at least 5% of baseline weight at 68 weeks, regardless of treatment discontinuation or rescue intervention. Published on 10 February 2021: 1,961 adults without diabetes were randomized to subcutaneous semaglutide 2.4 mg weekly (n=1,306) or placebo (n=655), plus lifestyle intervention. Mean weight changes were −14.9% versus −2.4%; observed ≥5% losses were 1,047/1,212 versus 182/577 among participants measured at week 68. Both coprimary comparisons had P<0.001.
milestones.set_by: Novo Nordisk, STEP 1 protocol NCT03548935 and its prespecified analysis, described in the trial report; semaglutide-specific.
milestones.threshold_quote: All results from statistical analyses were accompanied by a two-sided 95% confidence interval and corresponding P values (with significance defined as P<0.05).

milestones.title: An obesity medicine receives FDA approval for chronic weight management.
milestones.criterion: FDA approves chronic weight management in adults with initial body mass index at least 30 kg/m², or at least 27 kg/m² with at least one weight-related comorbidity, as an adjunct to a reduced calorie diet and increased physical activity. Body mass index is weight in kilograms divided by height in metres squared. Wegovy (semaglutide) injection received this approval on 4 June 2021.
milestones.set_by: U.S. Food and Drug Administration, original Wegovy approval NDA 215256 and prescribing information, section 1; these eligibility thresholds are from the adult semaglutide indication.
milestones.threshold_quote: WEGOVY is indicated as an adjunct to a reduced calorie diet and increased physical activity for chronic weight management

milestones.title: Semaglutide reduces the cardiovascular death, nonfatal infarction or stroke composite with P<0.046.
milestones.criterion: SELECT required superiority for time to first cardiovascular death, nonfatal myocardial infarction or nonfatal stroke, using a group-sequential design with overall one-sided type I error 0.025 and final nominal two-sided P<0.046. Participants were ≥45 years old, had body mass index ≥27 kg/m² and established cardiovascular disease, and had no diabetes. Published on 11 November 2023: subcutaneous semaglutide 2.4 mg weekly versus placebo, both with standard care, gave 569/8,803 (6.5%) versus 701/8,801 (8.0%) events; hazard ratio 0.80 (95% confidence interval 0.72–0.90), P<0.001, over mean follow-up 39.8 months.
milestones.set_by: Novo Nordisk and the SELECT academic steering committee, prespecified SELECT protocol NCT03574597 and group-sequential analysis; the final boundary is stated in the trial report's Table 2 footnote. Semaglutide-specific.
milestones.threshold_quote: the nominal two-sided significance level was 0.046.

results.finding: Semaglutide's nonclinical programme supported safety; animal sample sizes not reported for toxicology studies; monkey NOAEL was 0.06 mg/kg.
results.detail: FDA's signed review records the standard nonclinical programme reviewed under IND 79754 and NDA 209637 and reused for obesity development. It concludes that the nonclinical data support market approval; this is not itself an approval decision.
results.quote:
The nonclinical data support market approval of subcutaneously administered 
semaglutide as an adjunct to a reduced calorie meal plan and increased physical 
activity for chronic weight management in adult patients with obesity or excess weight.

results.finding: Semaglutide reduced body weight in diet-induced obese rats over 77 days; animal sample size was not reported.
results.detail: The excerpt reports nonclinical pharmacological results and an ICH-aligned safety programme, but no toxicological findings or conclusion that proposed human investigations were reasonably safe under 21 CFR 312.23(a)(8).
results.quote:
Subcutaneous doses of 1.2 and 4.1 μg/kg once-daily for 77 
days led to a dose-dependent, significant decrease in body weight, primarily from fat.

results.finding: In STEP 1, semaglutide outperformed placebo on both coprimary weight endpoints at 68 weeks in 1,961 adults without diabetes (two-sided P<0.001 for both).
results.detail: Participants received weekly subcutaneous semaglutide 2.4 mg or placebo plus lifestyle intervention. The treatment policy estimand included treatment discontinuation and rescue intervention. Mean weight changes were −14.9% versus −2.4%; observed ≥5% losses were 1,047/1,212 versus 182/577.
results.quote:
Statistical superiority of 
semaglutide over placebo was achieved for all 
end points in the hierarchical testing procedure.

results.finding: FDA approved Wegovy (semaglutide) for chronic weight management on June 4, 2021; sample size not reported.
results.detail: Approved as an adjunct to a reduced calorie diet and increased physical activity in adults with initial BMI ≥30 kg/m², or ≥27 kg/m² with at least one weight-related comorbid condition.
results.quote:
We have completed our review of this application, as amended. It is approved, effective 
on the date of this letter, for use as recommended in the enclosed agreed-upon 
labeling.

results.finding: SELECT: semaglutide reduced the primary cardiovascular composite versus placebo in 17,604 adults; two-sided P<0.001.
results.detail: Adults ≥45 years with BMI ≥27 kg/m², established cardiovascular disease and no diabetes received weekly subcutaneous semaglutide 2.4 mg or placebo with standard care. Hazard ratio 0.80 (95% CI 0.72–0.90); mean follow-up 39.8 months. The result passed the group-sequential final nominal significance threshold of 0.046.
results.quote:
A primary cardiovascular end-point event occurred in 569 of the 
8803 patients (6.5%) in the semaglutide group and in 701 of the 8801 patients 
(8.0%) in the placebo group (hazard ratio, 0.80; 95% confidence interval, 0.72 to 
0.90; P<0.001).

results.finding: FDA approved Wegovy to reduce major cardiovascular events on 8 March 2024, based on SELECT; the letter specifies approximately 17,500 planned patients.
results.detail: The approved indication covers adults with established cardiovascular disease and obesity or overweight. SELECT is described as randomized, double-blind and placebo-controlled, comparing semaglutide 2.4 mg with placebo. The letter does not report actual enrollment or event rates.
results.quote:
We have completed our review of this application, as amended. It is approved, effective 
on the date of this letter, for use as recommended in the enclosed agreed-upon labeling 
with minor editorial revisions listed below and reflected in the enclosed labeling.
